prompt: Run the llm-working2grid ablation baseline for as-jpn-tokyo-jr-shape-rect (orig). Decide every cell by reasoning point by point; do not generate coordinates algorithmically.

transcript.note:
Round 1, laid out from scratch off geography alone (no baseline here). 97 points, 175 segments, 132 intermediate stations left to placeBlacks.
Design: this chain has no control to beat and no drift numbers, so I aimed at the compact end of the trade-off - the tightest grid I could hold together (29x32 for 97 points) with as many segments straight as possible, and I checked criterion 3 by hand off gx/gy.
1) Interchanges first (criterion 1): I fixed every deg>=3 point onto a column band ordered by gx and a row band ordered by gy, so no east/west or north/south relation could invert by construction, then merged adjacent bands wherever the merge bought a straight segment and cost no collision.
2) One line one direction (criterion 2): Shinjuku Line is a single horizontal (Nishi-shinjuku-gochome/Tochomae/Shinjuku/Shinjuku-sanchome/Ichigaya at row 15, then Kudanshita/Jimbocho/Ogawamachi/*82/Akihabara at row 17); Hanzomon a single horizontal at row 13 (Otemachi-*83-Mitsukoshimae-Ningyocho); Oedo a single horizontal at row 20 (Kasuga-Hongo-sanchome-*94-Naka-okachimachi-*87); Yamanote's west side is one vertical in column 9 (Takadanobaba-*86-Shinjuku-Yoyogi-*95-Shibuya) and its north side one horizontal at row 23 (Ikebukuro-Sugamo-Komagome-Nishi-nippori); Fukutoshin one vertical in column 10; Marunouchi one vertical in column 16 (Ginza-Tokyo-Otemachi-Ogawamachi).
3) Chains built specifically for this layout: Meguro-Shirokane-takanawa-Mita is a horizontal at row 2 continuing Naka-meguro-Ebisu-Meguro, and column 12 carries Shirokane-takanawa/Azabu-juban/Roppongi/*93 as one vertical; Daimon-Shimbashi-Yurakucho is one vertical in column 15 with Shimbashi levelled to *96; Higashi-nihombashi lifted to the Morishita/Sumiyoshi row; Motohachiman and Nishi-funabashi pulled onto the Funabori and Minami-gyotoku columns.
4) Where I lost: cross=2, both the Mita Line (Shirokane-takanawa-Mita-*84) against the contracted Yamanote chord Gotanda-Daimon. That pair is forced, not sloppiness - the hard rule at Daimon requires Mita south of that chord and *84 north of it, so Mita-*84 has to cross it, and moving Shirokane-takanawa south instead just relocates the crossings onto its other two edges. The compactness also cost fidelity: squeezing 97 points into 29x32 pulls the sparse south and east inward, and my own check finds 11 pairs whose clear east/west or north/south relation inverted (all of them one band apart, none across the middle of the map).
